clue.text: Set sailor free

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
solute is an old and botanical word for loose or free, not attached

explanation.surface: An order to release a captive seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set ... free' reads as one phrase meaning release, but 'Set' is the definition and 'free' gives SOLUTE, a rare word for unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolute is fixed and definite, as a set rule or decision is.

clue.text: A duchess's place at Italian resort

parts.note: Webster's tragedy The Duchess of Malfi names her duchy

explanation.surface: A noblewoman's home is in an Italian holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: The duchess is Webster's Duchess of Malfi.
explanation.definitionFit: Amalfi is a resort town on the coast south of Naples.

clue.text: One who got the silver back

definitions.meaning: the runner-up wins the silver medal
to back is to support, as one does a motion

explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up comes in behind the winner; to support a proposal is to back it.

clue.text: Girl told to come home

definitions.meaning: a Scottish word for a young woman
the collie of the film ... Come Home

explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a young woman, and the famous film collie ordered home in Lassie Come Home.

clue.text: Eat hotpots rehashed — then use this

indicators.note: a rehash is a reworking, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: After eating reheated stew, clean your teeth with this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rehashed' rearranges EATHOTPOTS; a hotpot is a British stew of meat under sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste for cleaning teeth is what one uses after a meal.

clue.text: Rough butcher has no time for baby-faced child

indicators.note: roughed up, the letters are knocked out of their order
the word butcher loses one letter for time

explanation.surface: A coarse meat trader is said to be impatient with a cute youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no time' takes T out of BUTCHER, leaving BUCHER, which 'Rough' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a chubby, angelic-looking infant, as in Renaissance paintings.

clue.text: Top post! It's the Admiral's

definitions.meaning: the position of being in charge, as of a school
split into two words, the admiral's own vessel would be the leading vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The office of a head teacher or chief is a top post; read as two words, the leading vessel of a fleet.

clue.text: Mad behaviour of people on the way

definitions.text: Mad behaviour of people on the way

parts.words: Mad behaviour of people on the way
parts.note: seems to describe travellers or pilgrims, but means drivers losing their temper on the road

explanation.definitionFit: Violent fury shown by motorists towards other drivers is this.

clue.text: Drinking song sung on the 25?

definitions.meaning: a toast, set to music in opera
25 across is the Adriatic, on whose shore this port lies; sung hints at the song sense

explanation.definitionFit: A toast song in Italian opera, and a port on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Acorn set to become start of tree

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An acorn is planted to grow into the beginning of an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges ACORNSET. The tree is a family tree, not an oak.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor stands at the root of a family tree, where the lineage begins.

clue.text: Country where I'm a lawbreaker?

indicators.note: the words are broken up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A criminal wonders which nation he is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaker' breaks up IMALAW; 'lawbreaker' looks like one word but splits as fodder plus indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Cool, pale source of illumination

parts.note: to fan is to cool with moving air
light colours are pale ones

explanation.surface: A cool, pale lamp lights a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a semicircular window above a door that lets daylight in.

clue.text: Girl almost has a leg in each side

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.words: has a leg in each side
parts.note: to sit astride something is to have a leg on each side of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter E from ASTRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a Scandinavian female first name.

clue.text: Old reptile flying near to pond

indicators.note: the letters take flight and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient creature swoops low over water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges NEARTOPOND and suits the flying reptile itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pteranodon was a large flying reptile of the Cretaceous period.

clue.text: Birds nesting in some high places

parts.note: part means some of something
ridges are long raised stretches of land

explanation.surface: Birds make their nests on lofty crags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nesting in' is only the link of the surface; partridges in fact nest on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Partridges are plump game birds of farmland.

clue.text: Notting Hill's, perhaps, can rival Rio's

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: London's street party may match Brazil's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CANRIVAL. Notting Hill, in London, holds a Caribbean street festival each August; 'Rio's' rounds off the surface with Brazil's famous one.
explanation.definitionFit: Notting Hill's famous yearly street festival goes by this name, as does the one in Rio.

clue.text: Place of ups and downs for the traveller

definitions.text: Place of ups and downs for the traveller

parts.words: Place of ups and downs for the traveller
parts.note: sounds like hilly country or a life of fortune, but means where planes take off and land

explanation.definitionFit: Places where aircraft take off and land are where flyers go up and come down.

clue.text: Joyce was one name on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to dub is to give a name
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: James Joyce was a name painted on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Joyce is the novelist James Joyce, born in Dublin, who also wrote the stories Dubliners.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce was a native of the Irish capital, so a citizen of it.

clue.text: Bringing up workers in a religious environment

parts.note: pi is a slang short form of pious
a culture is the medium or environment in which something is grown

explanation.surface: Raising staff within a churchy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are worker bees, not factory hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is beekeeping, the rearing of honeybees, which include the worker caste.

clue.text: State car used by Italian resort

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A government vehicle used in an Italian seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a resort on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Bats in strange lament

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Flying mammals feature in a weird dirge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges LAMENT; 'Bats' is slang for crazy, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for crazy, as is mental.

clue.text: "They're ruined!", said the King

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, used in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A monarch declares that something is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruined ships, cars or buildings are wrecks.

clue.text: Italian city in a police state

indicators.note: to state is to put into words, and the words here voice the city's letters inside them

explanation.surface: An Italian city lies within an authoritarian regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The city runs through 'iN A POLIce'; 'state' looks like the end of 'police state' but signals the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoli is the Italian name for Naples, the great southern city.

clue.text: American whose job is on the line

definitions.text: American whose job is on the line

parts.words: American whose job is on the line
parts.note: reads as a worker facing dismissal, but in US usage the driver of a railway locomotive, who works on the railway line

explanation.definitionFit: In American English the driver of a train is called by this title.

clue.text: Italian setting for gentlemen lovers

parts.note: points to the Shakespeare comedy about two gentlemen in love, named after their Italian home city

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare set The Two Gentlemen of Verona there, and Romeo and Juliet too.

clue.text: The main threat to Venice: mad raid by heartless Greek

indicators.note: the word raid goes wild and its letters scatter
the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, so Greek

explanation.surface: Venice is endangered by a crazed attack from a cruel Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns RAID into ADRI; 'heartless' removes the middle T of ATTIC to give ATIC. The main is the sea, whose floods threaten Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the sea whose high tides flood Venice.

clue.text: Ulster in turmoil for five years

indicators.note: in chaos, the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland endured half a decade of strife.
explanation.walkthrough: ULSTER, the northern province of Ireland, is rearranged by 'in turmoil'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustre, or lustrum, is a period of five years, from the Roman census.

clue.text: Islands more or less in the Caribbean

definitions.text: Islands more or less in the Caribbean

parts.words: Islands more or less in the Caribbean
parts.note: 'more or less' seems to mean roughly, but refers to the Greater and Lesser groups of Caribbean islands

explanation.definitionFit: The Greater and Lesser groups of Caribbean islands share this name.
